transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alice Monroe (Redwood AE), Jonah Park (Redwood SE), Sara Gupta (Lucid CISO), Mark Lee (Lucid CTO), Priya Nair (Lucid Infra)

Summary: quick security posture discovery focusing on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs and KMS/encryption. Customer has regulated ML workloads and strong data residency needs.

[00:00] Alice Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alice, AE for Redwood. Jonah our SE is here too. 
[00:12] Sara Gupta: Thanks, Alice. I'm Sara, CISO at Lucid Systems. We wanted to do a security-first discovery to understand where Redwood fits for our inference needs.
[00:20] Jonah Park: Hi all, Jonah here. We'll focus on architecture options (hosted, dedicated, private) and controls — SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, retention.
[00:30] Mark Lee: Quick context — we run PII/PHI-ish data through inference for analytics, so compliance and residency are heavy constraints. Expecting production latency ~100ms tail for short prompts.
[00:45] Priya Nair: And we have a hybrid infra: some models run in our VPC, some in cloud. We prefer to avoid sending raw PII off-prem unless encrypted or tokenized.
[00:55] Alice Monroe: Totally understood. To frame options: Hosted (fastest onboarding) — Redwood-managed, SOC2 in our compliance pack, encryption, tenant isolation. Dedicated — reserved GPU pools just for you with network controls and stronger SLAs. Private — VPC or on-prem where control plane can be customer‑managed. Each has slightly different sev of controls and data flow.
[01:20] Sara Gupta: Do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001? We need the actual reports to give to audit.
[01:27] Alice Monroe: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. I'll send the certs and the compliance pack after the call. They are in our security folder; we'll redact as needed.
[01:35] Mark Lee: For Hosted, what's the encryption at rest mechanism and KMS support? Can we bring our own key?
[01:42] Jonah Park: For hosted we support customer-managed KMS for workspace-level keys — you can BYOK via AWS KMS or Google CMEK. Data at rest is AES-256. For Dedicated and Private you get more control; Private can integrate with on-prem HSMs if needed.
[02:05] Priya Nair: Is that for model weights too or only customer data/cache? We cannot allow model artifacts containing sensitive vectors to be persisted outside our control.
[02:12] Jonah Park: We typically keep model binaries in object storage with access controls. For Private deployments, model artifacts live in your environment. For Dedicated we can provide options: ephemeral cache, or have you control buckets for model storage.
[02:35] Sara Gupta: Auditability — we need immutable audit logs of token access, who called endpoints, and traceability tied to SSO identity.
[02:43] Alice Monroe: We emit per-request logs with request id, user id, token usage, latency, and model version. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure streaming. Retention is configurable; default for hosted is 90 days, can be extended as an add-on.
[03:05] Mark Lee: How granular is RBAC? We want role separation between devs, MLOps, and security with least privilege.
[03:12] Jonah Park: RBAC supports role templates and custom roles — you can map your SAML groups to roles. For Private deployments you control the IdP integration. For Hosted we support SCIM for provisioning.
[03:30] Priya Nair: Speaking of SAML, any gotchas with SSO? We use Okta and Azure AD.
[03:35] Alice Monroe: Okta and Azure AD are both supported. SAML and OIDC both workable. We do SAML assertion mapping to internal roles; sometimes group sync timing causes transient access gaps — we recommend SCIM if you want near-real-time provisioning.
[03:50] Sara Gupta: Data retention: we need guaranteed deletion for certain data classes after 30 days and proof of deletion for audits. How do you handle that in Hosted?
[03:58] Jonah Park: For hosted we have retention controls per workspace. You can set retention policies and we support deletion requests; we return a deletion report. For stricter guarantees customers choose Dedicated or Private to keep all data in their buckets. Hosted can meet many customers' needs but some regulated customers choose Private for absolute control and chain-of-custody.
[04:25] Mark Lee: Network egress controls — can you restrict outbound access so models don't call external endpoints? We need to prevent exfil via webhooks.
[04:32] Alice Monroe: Yes, Private gives you full network control. For Dedicated we can implement strict egress rules per tenant and allowlist endpoints. Hosted has egress controls but more limited; we can work with you on webhooks via proxies.
[04:50] Sara Gupta: Are there attestation logs we can ingest into our audit? Like who viewed keys, who restarted nodes, etc?
[04:58] Jonah Park: We provide admin audit logs — key changes, role changes, deployment actions. Logs include actor, timestamp, action, and resource. For Private deployments those logs can be written to your syslog/S3 directly.
[05:15] Priya Nair: What about KV cache leakage — local caches storing prompt history — can those be encrypted with separate keys and purged?
[05:22] Jonah Park: Yes, KV caches are encrypted at rest and you can configure eviction/prefix caching policies. We can also support ephemeral caches per session in Private mode. There's a tradeoff between performance and retention.
[05:40] Sara Gupta: OK. On compliance, do you have pen test reports or third-party assessments?
[05:46] Alice Monroe: We do annual pen tests and can share redacted summaries under NDA. We also have a vulnerability management program and regular dependency scanning.
[06:00] Mark Lee: For Dedicated, how isolated is the hardware? Is it multi-tenant on the same GPU nodes or fully reserved?
[06:07] Jonah Park: Dedicated is isolated GPU pools reserved to your account — no tenant mixing on those nodes. Some control plane components remain multi-tenant, but we maintain strong isolation and network policies.
[06:23] Sara Gupta: For our SOC team, we need a network diagram showing where data flows for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[06:29] Alice Monroe: We'll include network diagrams in the pack. We'll annotate where keys live, how telemetry flows, and retention points.
[06:38] Priya Nair: Latency tests: can you run a sample with our test token set to validate 100ms tail?
[06:44] Jonah Park: We can run a benchmark; for Hosted we'll run in-region tests. For Dedicated/Private we'll run against a test deployment. I'll coordinate with Priya to schedule and run with your sample prompts.
[07:00] Mark Lee: Any known limitations with on-prem HSM integrations?
[07:06] Jonah Park: HSM integrations are typically via KMIP or vendor-specific connectors; we recommend a short POC for HSM handshake, cert provisioning, and latency profiling.
[07:20] Sara Gupta: Encryption of in-flight data — TLS? Mutual TLS?
[07:24] Alice Monroe: TLS 1.2/1.3 everywhere. Mutual TLS supported for specific customer endpoints, and we can support private link/VPC endpoints to avoid public internet exposure.
[07:40] Priya Nair: What's the default retention policy for logs and tokens? You said 90 days default for hosted; can you keep audit logs for 1 year?
[07:47] Jonah Park: Yes, audit log retention is configurable as an add-on — 1 year or longer with archival to your storage.
[07:55] Sara Gupta: Data residency — we need processing to occur in EU for EU customers. Do you have regional hosting?
[08:02] Alice Monroe: We have regions in NA and EU; you can pin workloads to region. For Private you can deploy entirely in your on-prem region.
[08:15] Mark Lee: Cost question — does Dedicated/Private add significant ops overhead? From a security team viewpoint we prefer Private, but budget might push us to Dedicated.
[08:24] Alice Monroe: Dedicated provides a middle ground — strong isolation with lower ops cost than full Private. We'll provide cost/benefit guidance in the follow-up including the expected unit cost delta and ops responsibilities.
[08:40] Priya Nair: On SSO provisioning, do you offer SCIM or just SAML group mapping?
[08:45] Jonah Park: We support SCIM for provisioning with Hosted and Dedicated. Private can be set up to use your internal provisioning.
[08:55] Sara Gupta: Incident response — do you have a documented IR plan and can you share SLA for incident notification?
[09:02] Alice Monroe: Yes, we have an IR plan and defined notification timelines; for customers with enterprise SLAs we offer faster notifications and a dedicated responder option. We'll include the IR summary in the pack.
[09:18] Mark Lee: Are logs tamper-resistant? Can we use WORM storage for certain artifacts?
[09:22] Jonah Park: We can write logs to your WORM-capable buckets for immutability. Hosted can export to your S3 with WORM policies enforced on your side.
[09:40] Sara Gupta: Any regulatory evidence for HIPAA or SOC specific to healthcare?
[09:46] Alice Monroe: We aren't a HIPAA-covered entity, but we do support customers operating under HIPAA — we have BAA options for Dedicated/Private and controls that help customers demonstrate compliance.
[10:05] Priya Nair: Regarding model outputs, do you support redaction or tokenization before writing to logs to avoid PII in trails?
[10:12] Jonah Park: Yes — you can enable PII scrubbing on outputs and we can redact or hash sensitive spans before persistence. For high assurance customers we recommend doing scrubbing client-side or in a preprocessing layer.
[10:30] Sara Gupta: Good. Let's talk about the proof-of-concept — timeline and success criteria.
[10:34] Alice Monroe: Typical POC: 4 weeks, objectives: achieve <100ms 95th percentile for target prompt set, validate key rotation and KMS integration, validate SSO provisioning, and ensure retention/deletion flows.
[10:45] Mark Lee: That aligns. We'll want a contract clause for data residency and breach notification around 24 hours.
[10:52] Alice Monroe: We can include tighter breach notification terms in enterprise SLA.
[11:00] Priya Nair: Any limitations on model quantization or running proprietary models on Private?
[11:06] Jonah Park: Private supports your proprietary models and quantization options; some optimizations are hardware-specific, but we can test during POC.
[11:20] Sara Gupta: For the audit team, we'll need the matrix: control -> evidence -> where it's stored. Can you provide that?
[11:26] Alice Monroe: Yes we'll produce a controls matrix mapping SOC2/ISO controls to evidence artifacts and locations.
[11:35] Mark Lee: Are you able to provide a sample contract clause for data deletion and egress costs?
[11:40] Alice Monroe: We'll include sample contract language and outline egress pricing.
[11:48] Priya Nair: One more — do you support tenant-scoped encryption keys so each team in our org can have different keys?
[11:55] Jonah Park: Yes, multi-tenant key scoping is supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports workspace-level keys which map to teams.
[12:08] Sara Gupta: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[12:11] Alice Monroe: Recap: I'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, network diagrams, IR summary, compliance pack. Jonah will schedule a technical deep dive and run a latency POC once Priya shares sample prompts. Priya will share retention policy and any regulated dataset list.
[12:28] Mark Lee: We'll review and come back with access requests.
[12:31] Alice Monroe: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with proposed POC timeline and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
